title: A Orchard for the Regiment
premise: In the garrison city of Vellamere, Rosalind Zhou, a mapmaker's apprentice, is completing the great atlas her master died protecting when an abandoned child arrives at the workshop door carrying a sealed note: forget the face. The child's face, it turns out, matches a bloodline the ruling Regiment has spent thirty years erasing — and the atlas itself contains the only surviving proof. As soldiers close in on the workshop, Rosalind must choose between finishing the master's work and saving the child, discovering that the map's final blank page was left for them to fill with the truth. In the end, Rosalind smuggles the atlas out through the old orchard tunnels beneath the city, publishes it under the dead master's name, and gives the child both a new identity and the inheritance of the old one.
about_author: Xanthe Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated maps in colonial record offices before turning to fiction. Their novels explore what paper remembers that people are made to forget.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In the drafty workshop of the late Master Aldous Fen, Rosalind grinds pigments and traces coastlines for the unfinished Vellamere Atlas, telling themselves history happens elsewhere. The emotional beat is quiet grief disguised as diligence — they measure everything except their own loss.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A boy of six or seven appears on the step at dawn, wrapped in a soldier's cloak, with a note reading 'forget the face.' Rosalind takes him in against every instinct of self-preservation. The beat is reluctant tenderness blooming where fear should be.

chapters.title: The Face That Matches
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with a flashback to Master Fen's last weeks. Cleaning the boy's cut brow, Rosalind recognizes his features from a defaced portrait plate hidden in the atlas folio — the extinguished Aurelian line. The beat is dawning dread: the past has just walked into the present.

chapters.title: What the Master Died For
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Searching Fen's locked drawer, they find correspondence proving the Regiment ordered the atlas destroyed, not merely censored, and that Fen refused. The beat is furious clarity — the master's death was murder dressed as misfortune.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Courtesy Call
chapters.summary: Colonel Hesper Vance's POV. She inspects the workshop under pretense of condolence, probing for the atlas and measuring Rosalind's nerve. The beat is velvet menace; power shown as politeness with teeth.

chapters.title: Apprentice and Ward
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Days of hiding the boy — named Pip by his own insistence — inside the workshop while keeping production on schedule. Small joys: teaching him to draw compass roses. The beat is found-family warmth tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: The Orchard Below
chapters.summary: Pip's POV, simple and sensory. He discovers a hatch beneath the drying racks leading to orchard tunnels from the old city, and hears soldiers' voices below. The beat is childhood wonder curdling into intuition that adults lie.

chapters.title: Summons
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. An official writ demands the atlas be surrendered for 'imperial completion' within a fortnight. Rosalind realizes surrender means destruction and refusal means arrest. The beat is cornered resolve.

chapters.title: Ink and Ashes
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Working nights to finish the remaining plates, they find Fen's marginal notes pointing to the blank final page: 'for whoever inherits.' The beat is communion with the dead master across time.

chapters.title: Vance's Bargain
chapters.summary: Colonel Vance's POV. Offered promotion if she recovers the atlas intact, she weighs ambition against a flicker of doubt about the purge she helped execute. The beat is corruption rationalizing itself as duty.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A neighboring printer warns that someone inside the guild has reported the child's presence. Paranoia enters the workshop; Rosalind moves the atlas plates into the tunnels. The beat is trust fracturing.

chapters.title: Blood in the Margins
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Soldiers search the workshop while Pip hides in the pigment chest; he hears them discuss burning the 'last Aurelian evidence.' The beat is terror survived by stillness, innocence permanently altered.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Confronting the informant — an old friend of Fen's who traded information for his family's safety — Rosalind chooses mercy over exposure and gains an ally. The beat is compassion as strategy, forgiveness as resistance.

chapters.title: What's in a Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Researching the Aurelian line, Rosalind uncovers their own family's complicity: a grandfather who drew the original purge maps. Identity theme lands hard. The beat is shame transformed into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Fortnight Ends
chapters.summary: Colonel Vance's POV. The deadline passes; she orders the workshop seized at dawn but privately delays an hour, unable to say why. The beat is conscience flickering inside institutional machinery.

chapters.title: Fire
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Regiment burns the workshop; Rosalind and Pip escape into the orchard tunnels with the finished plates as twenty years of work goes up behind them. The beat is devastating release — losing everything except what matters.

chapters.title: Under the Roots
chapters.summary: Alternating Rosalind and Pip POVs. Lost in the tunnels, they follow Fen's coded survey marks toward the river gate, Pip's small courage steadying Rosalind's despair. The beat is mutual rescue across generations.

chapters.title: The Final Plate
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In a safehouse, Rosalind fills the atlas's blank last page: the true map of the purge, names and villages restored. The beat is authorship as inheritance — becoming the master by surpassing obedience.

chapters.title: Vance's Choice
chapters.summary: Colonel Vance's POV. Ordered to hunt the fugitives personally, she instead misfiles the tracking report, buying them a week and damning her career. The beat is a corrupt institution's servant choosing, too late, to be a person.

chapters.title: The Printing of Truths
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. With the informant-printer's help, the atlas is run off in secret editions overnight as patrols circle the district. The beat is breathless collective defiance — many hands making one truth.

chapters.title: An Orchard for the Regiment
chapters.summary: Climax, Rosalind's POV. Cornered at the river gate, Rosalind confronts Vance, offering her the atlas's dedication naming every officer who refused the order — including, now, hers. Vance lets them pass. The beat is power confronted not with force but with the record.

chapters.title: The Face Remembered
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue tone. A year later, the atlas circulates openly; Pip, given back his name Aurelian, chooses to keep 'Pip' anyway. Rosalind hangs Fen's compass above a new workshop door. The beat is inheritance redefined: we keep what we choose to carry.
